planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring or fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Bred by Hans A. Hansen and introduced through Walters Gardens, Cranberry Dancer brings a bold new color combination to the shade garden with cranberry-red sepals framing dark centers and bright yellow wingtips. The backs of the sepals reveal rosy-red tones edged in cream, giving a multi-tonal effect as the flowers nod and twist on wiry stems above the foliage in spring. This is a larger-growing epimedium than many compact cultivars, spreading into a substantial patch over time that suppresses weeds under deciduous trees. Cut back old foliage in late winter before new growth emerges to show off the spring flower display.

common_name: Hot Lips Epimedium (Bubblegum Pink Cranberry-Spurred Barrenwort)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring or fall in rich, well-drained soil in shade to part sun.

directions: An Epimedium acuminatum hybrid introduced by Diana Reek of Collector's Nursery, Hot Lips produces unusually large flowers with bright bubblegum-pink sepals and contrasting cranberry-red spurs, among the showiest blooms in the genus. The plant stays a well-behaved, tidy clump rather than spreading aggressively, and its foliage turns handsome shades of red and burgundy as temperatures cool in fall. Grow in light to full shade in average, rich, well-drained soil; it tolerates slightly more sun than many epimedium species. Cut back tattered winter foliage before new spring growth begins to best display the flowers.

common_name: Little Bo Peep Epimedium (Compact Chartreuse-Bronze Barrenwort)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring or fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Bred by Hans A. Hansen for Walters Gardens from a cross involving a proprietary Epimedium acuminatum selection, Little Bo Peep forms a compact, dense clump of semi-evergreen foliage that emerges light chartreuse with a bronze-burgundy blush in cool spring weather before settling to medium green for summer. Medium-sized flowers rise on panicles above the foliage in late spring, with pinkish-purple sepals and spurs tipped in light pink around rose-colored centers. Its small, tidy habit makes it well suited to the front of a shaded border, rock garden, or container planting where a full-sized epimedium would be too large. Cut back old foliage before new growth emerges in late winter for the best spring display.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring or fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Bred by Hans A. Hansen for Walters Gardens, Wisteria Falls is named for its cascading inflorescences, which can carry fifty to sixty pinkish-lilac flowers with wine-colored spurs per stem, reminiscent of a wisteria raceme in miniature. Each flower lasts about a week and is self-cleaning, extending the roughly three-week bloom display in late spring without the need for deadheading. Foliage emerges light chartreuse with a burgundy blush in cool weather, maturing to medium green through summer, with small marginal spines along the lanceolate leaflets. Grow in partial to full shade in humus-rich, well-drained soil for the fullest cascading flower show.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring or fall in rich, moist, well-drained woodland soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Bred by Hans A. Hansen for Walters Gardens, Dream Catcher carries rosy-red sepals that give way to large yellow wings, a bold bicolor flower on exceptionally long flower stems that produce blooms for many weeks in spring. Bright green leaves take on a moderate bronze cast in cool temperatures before greening up for summer. Compared to older epimedium cultivars, Dream Catcher was selected for larger flowers and sturdier flower stems, along with improved sun and drought tolerance once established. Grow in partial to full shade in rich, well-drained woodland soil; it will adapt to drier conditions under established trees.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring or fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Bred by Hans A. Hansen for Walters Gardens, Carnival Clown is one of the most vividly colored epimediums available, with vivid reddish-orange sepals surrounding spurs that have yellowish tips and bright orange centers. The evergreen, three-parted foliage has small marginal teeth and shows light chartreuse with bronze coloring in cool spring weather before becoming deep green through summer. Flower panicles appear in late spring above the foliage, giving a fiery contrast against the still-cool woodland garden palette. Grow in partial to full shade in well-drained, humus-rich soil, cutting back old foliage in late winter to show off the flowers.

common_name: Hugs and Kisses Epimedium (Deep Mauve Bicolor Pink Barrenwort)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring or fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade.

directions: A 2026 Walters Gardens introduction bred by Hans A. Hansen, Hugs and Kisses bears bicolor pink flowers with light pink backs and deep mauve centers, counted among the reddest epimedium flowers introduced to date. Burgundy flecking appears across the spring foliage, and slightly wavy leaf margins add texture beyond the bloom season. Like other epimediums it is semi-evergreen and does not require cutting back in regions where winter foliage persists, though removing tattered leaves in late winter will better showcase the spring flowers. Grow in partial to full shade in well-drained, humus-rich soil with low to average water needs once established.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring or fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Another 2026 Walters Gardens introduction bred by Hans A. Hansen, Woodland Elf produces soft yellow-tipped flowers with golden-yellow centers on scapes that are notably long, extending the bloom display well past the usual spring epimedium window. Elongated, lance-shaped foliage is heavily flecked with burgundy as it emerges in spring before settling to green. Like its relatives, it is semi-evergreen and does not need to be cut back, making it a low-maintenance, durable choice for shaded borders or a woodland garden floor. Grow in partial to full shade in well-drained, humus-rich soil for the best flowering display.
